name: Studio Lighting
author: Tequila
description: 21 ready-made product-photography studios - from clean e-commerce white and soft light tents to glass, jewellery, chrome and dramatic low-key sets. One click sets the lights, backdrop, floor and grade around your camera; your materials and camera are left alone. Every studio can then be fine-tuned: key, fill and rims, softness, warmth, gels, backdrop colour and glow, floor and reflections.

fields.text: Pick a studio and click Apply. Each one sets the lights, backdrop, floor and colour grade around your camera; your materials and the camera itself are left alone.
Swings the whole rig round the product. 0 = as the studio was designed, for your camera.
+1 is twice as bright, -1 half. Exposure only: the balance between the lights stays.
How strongly the studio's contrast, vignette, glow and colour grade apply. 0 = neutral, 100 = as designed, 200 = pushed.
Ctrl+Z undoes one Apply. More control: Plugins → Studio Lighting → Lights… and Backdrop & floor…
The main light: it shapes the product and casts its shadow.
Smaller = harder: crisp shadows, sharp highlights. Larger = softer, wrapping light. Its brightness stays the same.
Raise it for an overhead studio feel, lower it for long, dramatic side light.
Lifts the shadows, with the room's ambient light. 0 = deep shadows; more = flatter, cleaner light.
Edge lights behind the product that outline it against the backdrop.
The extras some studios add: sparkle lights for gems, halos, glows behind glass.
Tints the white lights: minus is cooler (blue), plus is warmer (amber). Coloured gels keep their colour.
Puts the key light, and everything else, on the other side.
Recolours the coloured lights of Cinematic Teal & Orange and Split Gel. A is the front or left gel, B the back or right one.
These carry over to every studio you apply until you reset them.
What's seen behind the product. My environment keeps your own HDRI behind and in the reflections, and only adds the studio's lights.
Used when Backdrop is Custom colour. The floor's shadows take its hue.
The pool of light on the backdrop straight behind the product. 0 = an even backdrop.
Shadows only: a seamless sweep. Satin and Glossy: soft or sharp reflections. Black mirror: a polished black table. No floor: the product floats.
How strongly the floor reflects the product.
The product's shadow on the floor. Off for a clean cut-out look.

fields.label: Place the lights around my camera

fields.text: On: the key is always on the same side of the picture. Off: the studio stays put in the scene, so orbiting shows it from other sides.
These carry over to every studio you apply until you reset them.
